sourceIssues.locator: Lemma 4.1, p. 12 of arXiv:2410.12560v1 and of the author manuscript (§4; published pp. 73–94, not read)
sourceIssues.printed: Let H be a finite group, let B be a finite H-module, let F be a field, and let V be a faithful H-representation over F. For every x ∈ V^{(1)}, let H_x ⊂ H be the stabilizer of x, and choose f_x ∈ F(V)^× such that div(f_x) = x. The group (B ⊗ F(V)^×)^H is generated by (B ⊗ F^×)^H and all elements of the form N_{H/H_x}(b ⊗ f_x), for all x ∈ V^{(1)} and all b ∈ B^{H_x}.
sourceIssues.correction: The lemma needs the hypotheses under which it is applied: that B is killed by n, that e(H) divides e and that F contains a primitive root of unity of order ne. With those hypotheses the statement is correct and is what the proof of Theorem 1.3 uses.
sourceIssues.reason: As printed the lemma is false, for two linked reasons. First, the elements N_{H/H_x}(b ⊗ f_x) need not lie in (B ⊗ F(V)^×)^H at all: f_x is determined only up to F^×, and for h ∈ H_x the ratio h(f_x)/f_x is a unit which need not be an nth power. Second, the proof reduces the statement to the generation of (B ⊗ Div(V))^H, which is correct, but that reduction needs the map (B ⊗ F(V)^×)^H → (B ⊗ Div(V))^H to be surjective, whereas taking H-invariants of the tensored divisor sequence is only left exact, as the displayed sequence in the proof itself shows. A counterexample: take F = R, H = C_2 = {1,σ} acting on V = A^1_R by t ↦ −t, which is faithful, B = Z/2 with trivial action, x the prime divisor (t) and f_x = t. Here H_x = H, so N_{H/H_x}(b ⊗ f_x) = 1 ⊗ t, and σ(1 ⊗ t) = 1 ⊗ (−t), which differs from 1 ⊗ t by the class of −1 in R(t)^×/(R(t)^×)^2. That class is nontrivial: if −1 = (f/g)^2 with g ≠ 0 then f^2 + g^2 = 0, impossible because the leading coefficient of a nonzero sum of two squares of real polynomials is positive. So 1 ⊗ t is not H-invariant, and the asserted generating set is not contained in the group it is said to generate. The conclusion fails too, not only the statement's typing: an element of (B ⊗ F(V)^×)^H mapping to 1 ⊗ x would be the class of g = c·t·w^2 with c ∈ R^×, and σ(g)/g = −(σ(w)/w)^2 is a square only if −1 is, so the image of (B ⊗ F(V)^×)^H in (B ⊗ Div(V))^H does not contain 1 ⊗ x. The repair is available in the application: in the proof of Theorem 1.3 the paper checks that (h−1)f ∈ μ_e for h ∈ H_x, and since μ_{ne} ⊂ F every element of μ_e is an nth power in F^×, so b ⊗ f is H_x-invariant when nB = 0 and the orbit generators do lift. Theorem 1.3 and everything after it are therefore unaffected; what fails is the unrestricted statement of Lemma 4.1.

sourceIssues.locator: §2, the display (2.3) and the words introducing it, p. 6 of arXiv:2410.12560v1 and of the author manuscript
sourceIssues.printed: gives a transgression map (2.2) tg: H^1(L,A)^H → H^2(H,A) fitting into a short exact sequence (2.3) H^1(L,A)^H →^{tg} H^2(H,A) →^{inf} H^2(L,A).
sourceIssues.correction: "fitting into an exact sequence", with the last term H^2(K,A): the sequence is exact at H^2(H,A) only.
sourceIssues.reason: Inflation for the extension 1 → Γ_L → Γ_K → H → 1 goes from cohomology of the quotient H to cohomology of Γ_K, so its target is H^2(K,A) and not H^2(L,A); the composite H^2(H,A) → H^2(K,A) → H^2(L,A) is in fact zero, so with the printed target the displayed sequence carries no information. That H^2(K,A) is meant is confirmed by the use made of the display: Corollary 2.4 is proved by combining it with Proposition 2.1, whose last assertion is H^2(H,A)_{neg,F} = Ker[H^2(H,A) →^{inf} H^2(F(V)^H,A)], and F(V)^H is the field K of the display. The sequence is also not short exact: it is the relevant segment of the five-term exact sequence of the Lyndon–Hochschild–Serre spectral sequence, which asserts only Im(tg) = Ker(inf); tg need not be injective and inf need not be surjective, and the display has no zeros at its ends. Both slips are harmless because only exactness at the middle term is used.

sourceIssues.locator: Proof of Lemma 2.5, the final displayed chain of equalities, p. 7 of arXiv:2410.12560v1 and of the author manuscript
sourceIssues.correction: cor^{H'}_H(tg(x)) = −cor^{H'}_H(u' ∪ x) = −u ∪ N_{H/H'}(x) = tg(N_{H/H'}(x)): the two classes u and u' = res^H_{H'}(u) are interchanged.
sourceIssues.reason: The proof has just established, from [NSW08, Theorem 2.4.4], that transgression for H is x ↦ −u ∪ x with u ∈ H^2(H,Δ) and that transgression for H' is x ↦ −u' ∪ x with u' = res^H_{H'}(u) ∈ H^2(H',Δ). The left-hand side applies the transgression for H', so the first equality must produce u', not u; and the projection formula [NSW08, Proposition 1.5.3(iv)] is cor(res(u) ∪ x) = u ∪ cor(x), so the middle term must have u, not u'. Each expression is individually ill-typed as printed: u ∪ x is not defined for x ∈ H^1(L,A)^{H'} regarded in H'-cohomology without first restricting u, and u' ∪ N_{H/H'}(x) lives in H^2(H',A) rather than in H^2(H,A), where the display says the identity holds. With the two swapped the chain is correct and the square of the lemma is proved.

sourceIssues.locator: Proof of Proposition 3.3, first paragraph, p. 11 of arXiv:2410.12560v1 and of the author manuscript
sourceIssues.printed: We apply Lemma 3.4 to the short exact sequence (3.2) and conclude that for every f ∈ L^× such that fμ_e ∈ (L^×/μ_e)^H we have (∂_2∂_1)(fμ_e) ∈ Im[H^2(H,Z) ⊗ μ_n →^∪ H^2(H,μ_n)].
sourceIssues.reason: Lemma 3.4 is stated for a short exact sequence 0 → X → Y → Z → 0 of abelian groups regarded as H-modules with trivial action, and concludes that Im(H^1(H,Z) →^∂ H^2(H,X)) is contained in the image of the cup product H^2(H,Z) ⊗ X → H^2(H,X). The sequence (3.2) is 1 → μ_e → L^× → L^×/μ_e → 1, in which H acts on L^× through the Galois action and not trivially, so the lemma does not apply to it; moreover its connecting map is ∂_1, with target H^1(H,μ_e), not the ∂_2 whose image the conclusion is about. The sequence to which the lemma does apply, and which gives exactly the stated conclusion, is (3.3), that is 1 → μ_n → μ_{ne} → μ_e → 1, whose three terms carry the trivial H-action because μ_{ne} ⊂ K, with X = μ_n, Y = μ_{ne}, Z = μ_e and the class ∂_1(fμ_e) ∈ H^1(H,μ_e). The intended reading is unambiguous and the conclusion is correct.

sourceIssues.locator: Proof of Lemma 5.3, second and third sentences, p. 15 of arXiv:2410.12560v1 and of the author manuscript
sourceIssues.printed: Let E ⊂ GL(Ṽ ⊕ W̃) be the inverse image of GL(V) ⊂ GL(V ⊕ W). The restriction to Ṽ of any element of E belongs to GL(Ṽ). It follows that restriction to Ṽ defines a group homomorphism π: E → GL(Ṽ).
sourceIssues.correction: An element of E need not preserve Ṽ. The map π is the top-left block, g = [[A,B],[C,D]] ↦ A, and it is a homomorphism because the off-diagonal blocks B and C of any g ∈ E are divisible by p, so that all their products vanish modulo p^2.
sourceIssues.reason: E is the inverse image of the subgroup GL(V) ⊂ GL(V ⊕ W), embedded as g ↦ diag(g, id_W). An element of E therefore reduces modulo p to a block diagonal matrix, which says that its off-diagonal blocks are divisible by p, not that they vanish. Concretely, with Ṽ of rank two and W̃ of rank one inside (Z/p^2)^3, the matrix I + pE_{31} lies in E, since it reduces to the identity, and it does not preserve Ṽ: it sends the first basis vector to e_1 + p e_3. So restriction to Ṽ is not defined on E and the printed justification fails. The map g ↦ A is nevertheless well defined and multiplicative: writing g = [[A,pB'],[pC',D]] and h likewise, the top-left block of gh is A_gA_h + p^2 B'_gC'_h = A_gA_h in Z/p^2, and A is invertible because it reduces to an element of GL(V). With that replacement the diagram of the proof and the conclusion of the lemma are unchanged. The lemma is in any case also attributed to [DCF17, Lemma 3.4]; only the alternative argument the authors include is affected.

sourceIssues.locator: Proof of Claim 5.7, the paragraph beginning "Finally, we show that Im(ψ_Z)^T = 0", p. 19 of arXiv:2410.12560v1 and of the author manuscript (the paragraph starts at the foot of p. 18)
sourceIssues.printed: As T normalizes Z, the map ∂ is T-equivariant, and hence H^2(Z,Z) ≅ F_p(τ_13).
sourceIssues.reason: The T-action on characters is the contragredient one, and the proof says so explicitly a page earlier: (t·χ)(u) = χ(t^{-1}ut). For t = (t_1,t_2,t_3) and the generator σ_13 = I + E_13 of Z one has t^{-1}σ_13t = σ_13^{t_3/t_1}, so t·χ_13 = τ_31(t)χ_13 and H^1(Z,Q/Z) ≅ F_p(τ_31), hence so is H^2(Z,Z). The same convention is used correctly in the two neighbouring computations of the same proof, which give H^2(U,Z) ≅ F_p(τ_21) ⊕ F_p(τ_32) from χ_12 and χ_23, and H^2(N,Z) ≅ F_p(τ_21) ⊕ F_p(τ_31) from χ_12 and χ_13; the printed τ_13 is inconsistent with both. That τ_31 is meant is confirmed by the conclusion drawn two lines later, (A^Z ⊗ H^2(Z,Z))^T = ⟨E_13 ⊗ ∂(χ_13)⟩: since E_13 spans the τ_13-weight line of A, the tensor is invariant exactly when the second factor has weight τ_31. With the printed τ_13 the invariants would vanish for every p > 3, contradicting the displayed answer. The parenthetical remark that follows, which distinguishes p > 3 from p = 3 by whether E_31 ⊗ ∂(χ_13) is also invariant, is correct for τ_31, because τ_13 and τ_31 coincide as characters of (F_3^×)^3 and not for larger p.

sourceIssues.locator: Proof of Claim 5.7, the last sentence of the paragraph showing Im(res^U_N ∘ φ_N)^T = 0, p. 18 of arXiv:2410.12560v1 and of the author manuscript
sourceIssues.printed: Since χ_12 extends to a character of U, by the projection formula φ_N(E_12 ⊗ ∂(χ_12)) belongs to the image of φ_U, and hence res^U_N(φ_U(E_12 ⊗ ∂(χ_12))) = 0 by the previous case.
sourceIssues.correction: the argument of φ_U must be N_{U/N}(E_12) ⊗ ∂(χ̃_12), where χ̃_12 is the character of U restricting to χ_12 and N_{U/N} = cor^N_U is the relative norm; that is, φ_N(E_12 ⊗ ∂(χ_12)) = φ_U(N_{U/N}(E_12) ⊗ ∂(χ̃_12)).
sourceIssues.reason: The map φ_U has source A^U ⊗ H^2(U,Z), and the proof has computed two paragraphs earlier that A^U = ⟨I, E_13⟩; the matrix E_12 does not lie in A^U, so the expression φ_U(E_12 ⊗ ∂(χ_12)) has no meaning. The projection formula, which is what the sentence invokes, produces the corrected expression: for a ∈ A^N and χ_12 = res^U_N(χ̃_12) one has φ_N(a ⊗ ∂χ_12) = cor^N_U(a ∪ res^U_N ∂χ̃_12) = cor^N_U(a) ∪ ∂χ̃_12 = φ_U(N_{U/N}(a) ⊗ ∂χ̃_12), and N_{U/N}(a) = cor^N_U(a) does lie in A^U. The conclusion is correct and in fact stronger than needed: conjugating E_12 by σ_23^i gives E_12 − iE_13, so N_{U/N}(E_12) = pE_12 − (p(p−1)/2)E_13 = 0 for odd p, whence φ_N(E_12 ⊗ ∂χ_12) = 0 outright.

sourceIssues.locator: Proof of Claim 5.6, first sentence, p. 17 of arXiv:2410.12560v1 and of the author manuscript
sourceIssues.printed: By definition, H̄^2(N,A) is generated by the images of all the φ_H, where H is a subgroup of U.
sourceIssues.correction: H̄^2(U,A) is generated by the images of all the φ_H, where H is a subgroup of U
sourceIssues.reason: The subgroup H̄^2(−,A) is defined after (3.7) as the subgroup of H^2(H,A) generated by the images of the maps φ_{H'} for the subgroups H' of the ambient group, and the maps φ_H for H ⊆ U land in H^2(U,A) by their definition (3.7), not in H^2(N,A). The claim being proved is about res^U_N(H̄^2(U,A)), and the rest of the proof decomposes H̄^2(U,A) by the order of H, so the ambient group is U throughout; the letter N in this one sentence is a slip. Nothing later depends on it.

sourceIssues.locator: Remark 5.8(2), p. 19 of arXiv:2410.12560v1 and of the author manuscript
sourceIssues.printed: (2) If the restriction of the class α to H^2(N,A) were not negligible over F, one could use this to simplify the proof of Theorem 5.1. However, this is not the case: one can show that α restricts to a negligible class in H^2(N,A).
sourceIssues.correction: The assertion is correct but no proof and no reference is given for it; a proof has to be supplied.
sourceIssues.reason: The remark asserts without argument that res^U_N(α) is negligible over F, which is the one place in the paper where a nontrivial cohomological fact is stated with only the words "one can show". The assertion is true and can be proved in two independent ways. Cohomologically: taking the least-residue section s(a,b) = I + āE_{12} + b̄E_{13} of N ≅ F_p^2 into GL_3(Z/p^2), all products of E_{12} and E_{13} vanish, so s(x)s(y)s(x+y)^{-1} = I + p(κ(a,c)E_{12} + κ(b,d)E_{13}) with κ(u,v) = ⌊(u+v)/p⌋ the carry; since the integral connecting class of the character a ↦ a/p mod Z is represented by that same carry, and N fixes both E_{12} and E_{13}, one gets res^U_N α = E_{12} ∪ δχ_{12} + E_{13} ∪ δχ_{13} in H^2(N,A), a sum of two generators of H̄^2(N,A) for the ambient group N, so Theorem 1.3 applies with e(N) = e(A) = p and μ_{p^2} ⊂ F. Directly: for any K/F and any continuous ρ = (χ_1,χ_2): Γ_K → N, Kummer theory lifts both characters to Γ_K → Z/p^2, and ρ̃(g) = I + χ̃_1(g)E_{12} + χ̃_2(g)E_{13} is a continuous homomorphism into GL_3(Z/p^2) lifting ρ, because the two matrix directions multiply to zero. Neither argument appears in the paper. Nothing in the paper depends on the remark: it is offered only to explain why the proof of Theorem 5.1 cannot be shortened by restricting to N, and Claim 5.4, which shows res^U_N(α) ≠ 0, is proved independently.
